title: Untrusted Input Triggering Nil Panic in Shared Service
platform_conditions: Go 1.x standard library; applies to all build targets (net/http recovers handler panics, but panics in user-spawned goroutines and non-net/http servers terminate the process)
security_mechanism: A failed type assertion without the ok form (x := v.(T)) panics; a write to a nil map panics; a nil pointer dereference panics. Unlike exceptions, a panic crosses goroutine boundaries unrecovered: net/http recovers panics inside its own handler goroutine, but any panic in a goroutine the handler spawned, or in a non-net/http service loop (custom TCP servers, gRPC streaming handlers), terminates the whole process. Because the input comes from the request, one malformed payload becomes a remote kill switch for every in-flight request.

source_sink_clues.source: Request bodies, headers, and decoded JSON/interface{} fields whose type or presence the client controls; missing fields decoded as nil.
source_sink_clues.sink: val := req.Body.(string) style single-value type assertions; writes to possibly-nil maps; index/slice expressions over untrusted indexes; goroutines spawned inside request handling without a recover

tracking_guards: Require the comma-ok assertion form (v, ok := x.(T)) with an explicit ok check before use; require nil-map initialization before writes; require untrusted-index bounds checks or get-with-ok accessors; require either a recover in every spawned goroutine or no goroutines on request paths that process untrusted data.
not_candidate_when: All assertions on untrusted values use the comma-ok form, the map is proven non-nil at write sites (initialized in the same function), the server recovers panics around every goroutine it spawns, or the value's type is guaranteed by an upstream decode into a concrete struct.
synthetic_safe_example: val, ok := req.Body.(string); if !ok { return nil, errors.New("invalid") }
public_references: CWE-755: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/755.html
Go standard library: builtin (type assertions, panic) — https://pkg.go.dev/builtin
